subject: Topic 2: Events from the Early 21st Century

topics.title: Mapping the Human Genome
passage: In 2003, scientists announced the completion of the Human Genome Project, a massive international effort to map every gene in human DNA. DNA acts like an instruction manual for the body, and the genome is the complete set of those instructions. Thousands of scientists from six countries worked together for thirteen years to read and record this incredibly detailed genetic code, which contains roughly three billion chemical letters.

Before this project, scientists could only study small pieces of DNA at a time, making it hard to understand how genes worked together. Once the full genome was mapped, researchers finally had a complete reference to compare against, which let them identify which genes were linked to certain diseases far more quickly than before. This shared map became a foundation that scientists all over the world could build on.

One major benefit of the Human Genome Project has been in medicine. Doctors can now test for genetic conditions more accurately, and researchers have developed treatments that target the specific genes involved in certain illnesses, an approach sometimes called personalized medicine. This means treatments can sometimes be tailored to a person's unique genetic makeup rather than using a one-size-fits-all approach.

The project also changed how quickly scientists could do this kind of research. When the Human Genome Project began, sequencing a small piece of DNA took a long time and a great deal of money. The technology developed during the project made the process faster and cheaper, and today a person's entire genome can be sequenced in about a day, something that would have seemed impossible before the project started.

The completion of the Human Genome Project is often compared to other major scientific milestones, like landing on the Moon, because of how it opened the door to new fields of research. Scientists continue to use the genome map today to study everything from ancient human history to the causes of rare diseases. Many researchers consider it one of the most important scientific achievements of the early 21st century.

topics.title: The Smartphone Revolution
passage: In January 2007, a new kind of phone was introduced that would change how people communicate, work, and entertain themselves. This device combined a phone, a music player, and an internet browser into a single pocket-sized gadget controlled almost entirely by touching the screen instead of pressing physical buttons. Within a few years, similar devices from other companies followed, and the smartphone quickly became one of the most widely used pieces of technology in the world.

Before smartphones, most cell phones could only make calls and send short text messages, and getting online usually meant sitting down at a desktop computer. Smartphones changed this by putting a powerful, connected computer in people's pockets. Suddenly, people could check email, look up directions, take photos, and browse the internet from almost anywhere, as long as they had a wireless signal.

One key part of the smartphone revolution was the app store, a place where people could download small programs, called apps, designed for specific tasks like games, weather forecasts, or banking. App stores allowed independent developers, not just large companies, to create new programs and reach millions of users. This opened the door to entirely new industries, including mobile gaming and ride-sharing services that did not exist before smartphones became common.

Smartphones also changed how people take and share photos and videos. Built-in cameras improved rapidly year after year, eventually becoming good enough that many people stopped using separate cameras altogether. Combined with new social media apps, people could instantly share pictures and videos with friends and family around the world, something that would have required much more time and equipment in the past.

Along with these benefits, smartphones brought new challenges, including concerns about screen time, privacy, and the difficulty of staying focused with constant notifications. Researchers and technology companies continue to study these effects and develop tools like screen-time trackers to help people manage their smartphone use. Even with these challenges, smartphones remain one of the most influential inventions of the early 21st century.

topics.title: The Rise of Social Media
passage: In the mid-2000s, a new kind of website began connecting people online in ways that had never been possible before. These social media platforms let users create personal profiles, share updates, post photos and videos, and connect with friends, family, and even strangers who shared their interests. Within just a few years, hundreds of millions of people around the world had joined these platforms, changing how people communicated on a massive scale.

Early social media sites focused mainly on connecting with people you already knew, such as classmates or coworkers, and sharing simple text updates or photos. As the technology improved, video-sharing sites emerged that let anyone upload and share videos with a worldwide audience, giving ordinary people a platform once available only to television networks and movie studios. This meant that everyday people could suddenly become widely known creators.

Social media also changed how news and information spread. Instead of waiting for a newspaper or television broadcast, people could share updates about events almost instantly with their entire network of followers. This speed had real benefits, such as quickly organizing charity efforts or spreading safety information during emergencies, but it also made it easier for incorrect information to spread quickly before it could be checked.

Businesses quickly recognized the value of social media as well, using these platforms to advertise products, communicate directly with customers, and build brand loyalty in ways that were not possible before. Small businesses, in particular, benefited from being able to reach potential customers without needing an expensive marketing budget. Social media became an essential part of how many companies operate today.

As social media grew, so did concerns about its effects, including the spread of misinformation, pressure related to comparing one's life to others online, and questions about how personal data is collected and used. Companies and researchers continue to study these issues and adjust platform features, such as flagging false information or offering tools to manage time spent online. Social media remains one of the most significant and debated developments of the early 21st century.

topics.title: New Horizons: A Journey to Pluto
passage: In January 2006, NASA launched a spacecraft called New Horizons on a journey to explore Pluto, a small, icy world at the edge of our solar system. At the time, Pluto had never been visited by any spacecraft, and much of what scientists knew about it came only from blurry telescope images taken from Earth. The trip to Pluto was so far away that New Horizons had to travel for more than nine years before it finally arrived.

New Horizons traveled roughly three billion miles to reach Pluto, moving faster than any spacecraft launched before it. To help it along the way, the spacecraft used a technique called a gravity assist, briefly swinging past the planet Jupiter in 2007 to gain extra speed, similar to how a slingshot works. This clever shortcut saved years of travel time compared to flying to Pluto directly.

On July 14, 2015, New Horizons finally flew past Pluto, capturing the first close-up images ever taken of its surface. Scientists were surprised to discover that Pluto had towering ice mountains, a huge heart-shaped plain of frozen nitrogen, and signs of geological activity, features that suggested Pluto was far more complex and active than many scientists had expected for such a small, distant world.

The mission also studied Pluto's largest moon, Charon, revealing canyons and cliffs that stretched for hundreds of miles across its icy surface. Because New Horizons could only fly past Pluto rather than orbit it, the spacecraft had just one close approach to gather as much data as possible, carefully capturing images and scientific readings during a flyby that lasted only a matter of hours.

After its flyby of Pluto, New Horizons continued deeper into a distant region of the solar system called the Kuiper Belt, where it flew past another small icy object in 2019. The mission changed how scientists think about small, distant worlds, showing that even objects far from the sun can have surprisingly active and complex geology. Data from New Horizons continues to be studied by scientists today.
